Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers

Source: R/attest.R
capsule_attest.Rd

capsule_attest() signs a manifest's canonical digest and records everything a verifier needs alongside it: the scheme, the public key, the context string, the pre-hash, a note and the signing time. capsule_check_attestation() checks the result against a manifest without being told anything further. Use them to publish a capsule together with proof that its manifest has not changed since you signed it.

Usage

capsule_attest(manifest, key, context = NULL, prehash = "none", note = NULL)

capsule_check_attestation(attestation, manifest, key_expected = NULL)

Arguments

manifest

A manifest, as from make_manifest().

key

A signing key from fips_keygen() (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and the other standardised schemes) or pqc_keygen() (XMSS).

context

Optional context string (or raw vector), bound into the signature for the standardised schemes; see capsule_sign(). NULL (the default) means none.

prehash

Pre-hash, as in capsule_sign(): "none" (the default) or a hash name such as "sha256" or "sha512".

note

Optional free text recorded in the attestation – what the signature is meant to assert, in the signer's own words. It is covered by the signature, since it is part of the digest.

attestation

An attestation from capsule_attest().

key_expected

Optional public key the attestation must carry: hex, or a key object from fips_keygen(), fips_public_key() or signing_public_key(). Supply it when you know which key should have signed: without it the check confirms the attestation is internally consistent, which any key's holder could arrange.

Value

capsule_attest() a list of class c("bricklayer_attestation", "list") with the character fields digest, scheme, public (hex), context, prehash, note and signed_utc (ISO 8601 UTC time), and signature (a bricklayer_signature from capsule_sign()). capsule_check_attestation() a list of class c("bricklayer_attestation_check", "list") with ok (logical) and checks, a data frame with columns check, ok and detail, one row per check.

Details

What this adds over capsule_sign(). A bare signature leaves three things implicit – which key, which scheme, and which bytes. A verifier who has to be told those out of band cannot check anything they were not already given, which makes the signature a formality. An attestation states them, so the check is capsule_check_attestation(attestation, manifest) and nothing else.

What is signed: the payload digest (manifest_digest() of the manifest), scheme, public, context (hex for a raw context), prehash, note and signed_utc is put in canonical form (manifest_canonical()) and its SHA-256 is signed with capsule_sign(). Every field, the note and the time included, is therefore covered: editing any of them breaks the signature. With an XMSS key from pqc_keygen() the scheme is "xmss-sha256" and the context and pre-hash are not used by the signature; signing uses up one of the key's one-time indices, as every XMSS signature does.

The check, one row each: attestation_complete (every field is present), manifest_digest (the manifest's digest equals the attested one), key_as_expected (only when key_expected is given) and signature (the signature verifies under the attested public key). ok is TRUE when every row passes.

What it does NOT establish. That the public key belongs to whoever you think it does: an attestation is only as good as the channel the key arrived on, which is why key_expected exists. And that the manifest is true – only that it has not changed since it was signed. capsule_falsify() is for the other question. No chain seal is recorded; to attest a run history, sign chain_seal() directly.

Errors: manifest not a list; key not from fips_keygen() or pqc_keygen(); an invalid prehash or context (from capsule_sign()); attestation not from capsule_attest(). A signature that fails to verify is a failed row, not an error.

See also

capsule_sign(), manifest_digest(), capsule_falsify(), chain_seal().

Examples

m <- make_manifest(list(dataset = "otis", rows = 1200L),
  environment = FALSE
)
key <- fips_keygen("ML-DSA-65")
att <- capsule_attest(m, key, note = "counts as published")
att
#> ── Capsule attestation ───────────────────────────────────────────
#>   scheme      ML-DSA-65
#>   digest      efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90
#>   context     <none>
#>   prehash     none
#>   note        counts as published
#>   signed      2026-10-15T20:59:20Z
#>   public key  132db7123cc11b3e93b324a465c93e06... (1952 bytes)
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# a verifier needs the attestation and the manifest, nothing else
res <- capsule_check_attestation(att, m)
res$ok
#> [1] TRUE
res$checks
#>                  check   ok
#> 1 attestation_complete TRUE
#> 2      manifest_digest TRUE
#> 3            signature TRUE
#>                                                             detail
#> 1                                                                 
#> 2 efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90
#> 3                                                                 

# any change to the manifest breaks it
m2 <- m
m2$meta$rows <- 1201L
capsule_check_attestation(att, m2)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# and so does presenting a different key
capsule_check_attestation(att, m,
  key_expected = fips_keygen("ML-DSA-65")$public
)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# the note is signed too: editing it breaks the signature row
forged <- att
forged$note <- "counts corrected"
capsule_check_attestation(forged, m)$checks[, c("check", "ok")]
#>                  check    ok
#> 1 attestation_complete  TRUE
#> 2      manifest_digest  TRUE
#> 3            signature FALSE

# a context string and a pre-hash
att2 <- capsule_attest(m, key, context = "release 2026-10", prehash = "sha512")
capsule_check_attestation(att2, m, key_expected = key)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# a key that is not a signing key is refused
try(capsule_attest(m, "not-a-key"))
#> Error : `key` must come from fips_keygen() or pqc_keygen()
